fleetMemory.LESSON: A pin whose two sides live in the same repo cannot fail on cross-repo drift, no matter how exact its assertion is - and the comment claiming otherwise is the thing that stops anyone looking. When a value is vendored across repos, the control has to read the OTHER repo's main, and the value must be extracted from the DEFINING module: a test's copy of a literal is itself a copy that can drift. Two controls failing on different things (in-repo pin for the lone edit, cross-repo check for the paired edit) is strictly better than one claiming both.

A push to one repo never re-runs the other's CI - the nightly schedule is the only thing that sees the one-sided edit nobody pushed over.
